# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your revenue reality, not your wishlist**
- Audit what your coaches actually deliver NOW (not what you want to offer). Map current class types, PT packages, add-ons (nutrition plans, form checks, challenges) and time investment per offering.
- Price reverse-engineered: calculate desired monthly revenue ÷ available coach hours = minimum price floor. Don't undercut this.

**2. Build two separate documents immediately**
- **Coach version**: what each service requires from them (prep time, messaging, follow-up), exact deliverables, which services they're authorized to sell. This kills confusion and upselling disputes.
- **Member version**: stripped of internal jargon. Use outcome language ("Build strength in 6 weeks" not "periodized resistance training"). Include what's *not* included (e.g., "nutrition coaching available separately").

**3. Test pricing with your current members this week**
- Don't guess. Run a 10-minute survey: show 2-3 price points for PT and ask "would you buy at £X?" Include a section asking what's missing from your current offering.
- Use responses to validate before finalizing.

**4. Create a one-page pricing anchor**
- Physical poster for gym + PDF for website. Simple table: service | duration | price | what's included. One format reduces coaching confusion and admin headaches.

**When**: Get the coach audit done this week. Menu finalized in 2 weeks. Saves you money on failed positioning later.

• **Revenue-per-member collapsed Oct (£106) after strong Sep (£138) — a 23% drop.** This isn't churn (members up 167) — it's pricing/product mix degradation. Action: run "premium class pass" upsell (£5–8 per session) on peak classes (likely 6–7pm weekday slots); test in Nov and project +£400/month if 10% conversion.

• **September peak (£22,016 rev on 159 members, £138/head) is your benchmark.** October dropped to £17,773 on higher headcount (167) — **this is the single biggest red flag.** New members in Oct are lower-value. Conservative: 40% of new Oct members = +£600 recurring if stacked in Nov.

• **Quiet class fill: no data provided, but with 159–167 members and (presumably) 12–16 weekly classes, utilisation is likely 60–70%.** Trial "buddy referral" incentive (£20 credit per friend who joins) targeting off-peak 10am/12pm slots; cost £20/head but converts £120+ ARPU over year. Pilot Nov, measure uptake.
